assessments.reasoning: The independently reacquired second-edition book names Mössenböck on physical page 1. The third paragraph of chapter 2, physical page 23, identifies Wirth’s Oberon as the language from which Oberon-2 evolved and describes type-bound procedures as the addition after Oberon’s type extension. The fourth paragraph distinguishes the language from the operating system. The contents on physical page 2 call the chapter opening page 13. Inspection of the full page image confirmed the absent printed folio. The actual adopter parent entity is the active base language anchored to Wirth’s 1 October 1990 report, which describes its Modula-2 lineage and type extension.

challenge.method: Test reversed direction, direct Modula-2 parentage, confusion with the operating system, and an assertion of equivalence between the book’s original citation and the registry’s exact 1990 edition. Inspect both original designer sources and the actual adopter entity.
challenge.results: The direct relationship is Oberon-2 → Oberon, with further predecessors earlier in the lineage. The operating system is separately identified. The book cites [ReW92], so its descriptive evidence identifies Wirth’s language and does not identify the registry’s 1990 PDF as its cited edition. That PDF independently identifies the registry target as the same base-language referent.

limitations: Mössenböck’s chapter is first-person co-designer documentation for descriptive lineage. The publisher notice on the PDF gives copyright 1993 and 1994. JKU’s catalogue distinguishes the English second edition as 1995. No equivalence of editions, code compatibility, runtime behavior, or dependence on the operating system was tested.
